topic: The drill nobody told you about
context: Tuesday 24 November, 4th period at {鷹ノ原高校|たかのはらこうこう}: an earthquake drill starts with the alarm sound, and アルちゃん, who never read the notice, runs for the door. {佐藤|さとう}先生 and {澪|みお} tell the story and give him advice on what to really do.
scene: Tuesday English class. A scary alarm goes off, and you run for the door. You were the only one who didn't know.

phrases.jp: {揺れて|ゆれて|to shake, sway|3}いる{時|とき}は、{外|そと}に{出ない|でない}ほうがいいですよ。
phrases.en: While it's shaking, you'd better not go outside.
phrases.note: 〜ないほうがいい = you'd better not. The classic earthquake rule: glass and roof tiles fall.

phrases.jp: {停電|ていでん|power cut|3}に{備えて|そなえて|to prepare for|3}、{懐中電灯|かいちゅうでんとう|torch, flashlight|3}を{用意|ようい}しておくといいよ。
phrases.en: It's a good idea to have a torch ready in case of a power cut.
phrases.note: 〜ておくといい = it's good to do in advance. Softer than 〜なさい.

phrases.jp: {天気予報|てんきよほう|weather forecast|3}によると、{明日|あした}は{大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}らしいよ。
phrases.en: According to the forecast, there's going to be heavy snow tomorrow.
phrases.note: 〜によると + らしい / そうだ: you say where you heard it.

phrases.jp: {避難所|ひなんじょ|evacuation shelter|2}の{場所|ばしょ}、{確認|かくにん}しといたら？
phrases.en: Why don't you check where the evacuation shelter is?
phrases.note: 〜たら？ = why don't you…? しといたら = しておいたら, casual.

phrases.jp: {地震|じしん|earthquake|4}の{時|とき}は、どうしたらいいですか？
phrases.en: What should I do in an earthquake?
phrases.note: どうしたらいいですか = what should I do? The easiest way to ask for advice.

dialogue_setting: Told afterwards by アルちゃん, {佐藤|さとう}先生 and {澪|みお}: class 2-3, 4th period, Tuesday 24 November.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: 4{時間目|じかんめ}の{英語|えいご}の{授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう}、スピーカーから{急|きゅう}に{怖い|こわい}{音|おと}が{鳴った|なった}。「{地震|じしん|earthquake|4}です！」
dialogue.en: In 4th-period English, a scary sound suddenly came from the speaker. 'Earthquake!'

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {僕|ぼく}は「{逃げなきゃ|にげなきゃ|to run away, escape|3}！」とドアに{走った|はしった}。でも{生徒|せいと|pupil, student|3}たちは{静か|しずか}に{机|つくえ}の{下|した}に{入って|はいって}いた。
dialogue.en: I thought 'I have to get out!' and ran for the door. But the students were quietly getting under their desks.

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: {実は|じつは|actually, the truth is|4}、{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん|evacuation drill|3}でした。アルちゃん{以外|いがい}は、みんな{知って|しって}いたんです。
dialogue.en: Actually, it was an evacuation drill. Everyone except アルちゃん knew.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {澪|みお}さんによると、{先週|せんしゅう}のプリントに{書いて|かいて}あったらしい。{僕|ぼく}だけ{読んで|よんで}いなかった…。
dialogue.en: According to {澪|みお}, it was written on last week's handout. I was the only one who hadn't read it…

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: {授業|じゅぎょう}の{後|あと}、{私|わたし}は{言いました|いいました}。「{揺れて|ゆれて|to shake, sway|3}いる{時|とき}は、{走らない|はしらない}ほうがいいですよ。{落ち着いて|おちついて|to calm down|4}{頭|あたま}を{守って|まもって}ください」
dialogue.en: After class I told him: 'While it's shaking, it's better not to run. Stay calm and protect your head.'

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: アルちゃん、ガチで{焦って|あせって}てウケたｗ　{非常用|ひじょうよう|for emergencies|3}の{水|みず}とライト、{家|いえ}に{置いとく|おいとく}といいっすよって{教えた|おしえた}。
dialogue.en: アルちゃん was seriously panicking, it was so funny lol. I told him it's good to keep emergency water and a light at home.
dialogue.note: ガチで = {本当|ほんとう}に, ウケた = {面白|おもしろ}かった, {置|お}いとく = {置|お}いておく, 〜っす = casual です.

listening.intro: On your way out of school, a voicemail from {恵子|けいこ}さん.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{恵子|けいこ}です。{帰り|かえり}に{電池|でんち|battery|3}、{買って|かって}きてくれる？{単三|たんさん|AA (battery size)|2}を4{本|ほん}ね。
lines.en: アルちゃん, it's {恵子|けいこ}. Could you buy batteries on the way home? Four AA.

lines.jp: {懐中電灯|かいちゅうでんとう|torch, flashlight|3}の{電池|でんち|battery|3}が{切れちゃった|きれちゃった|to run out|4}の。
lines.en: The torch batteries have run out.

lines.jp: {薬局|やっきょく|pharmacy|3}の{角|かど|corner|3}を{曲がった|まがった|to turn|4}ところの、{村井|むらい}さんのお{店|みせ}にあるよ。
lines.en: {村井|むらい}さん's shop has them, just round the corner from the pharmacy.

listening.question: {恵子|けいこ}さんは{何|なに}を{頼みました|たのみました}か。
options: {電池|でんち}を4{本|ほん}{買う|かう}こと
{懐中電灯|かいちゅうでんとう}を{買う|かう}こと
{薬局|やっきょく}で{薬|くすり}を{買う|かう}こと
{村井|むらい}さんに{電話|でんわ}すること
listening.explain: {電池|でんち}{買って|かって}きてくれる？{単三|たんさん}を4{本|ほん}: four AA batteries. The torch itself is fine; only its batteries ran out.

grammar.form: noun: + によると (ニュースによると, {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると) · person: + によると / の{話|はなし}によると ({澪|みお}さんによると, {先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}によると) · ending: + そうだ / らしい (…{降る|ふる}そうです, …あったらしい)
grammar.explanation: Names where information comes from: the news, a forecast, a notice, what someone said. The sentence usually ends in そうだ or らしい. Never use it for your own opinion (私によると ✗, say 私は〜と思う), and don't mix it up with によって (by, depending on).

examples.jp: ニュースによると、{白馬|はくば}のスキー{場|じょう}はもうオープンしたそうです。
examples.en: According to the news, the ski slopes in {白馬|はくば} have already opened.

examples.jp: {健太|けんた}の{話|はなし}によると、{駅前|えきまえ}に{新しい|あたらしい}ラーメン{屋|や}ができたらしい。
examples.en: According to {健太|けんた}, a new ramen shop has opened in front of the station.

quiz.question: ニュース＿＿、{明日|あした}は{雪|ゆき}が{降る|ふる}そうです。
quiz.en: According to the news, it's going to snow tomorrow.
quiz.explain: The news is the source of the information, so によると. について = about, にとって = for (someone).

quiz_more.question: {先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}によると、{訓練|くんれん|drill, training|3}は{来週|らいしゅう}＿＿。
quiz_more.en: According to the teacher, the drill is next week.
quiz_more.explain: A によると sentence ends with a hearsay form like そうです or らしい.

quiz_more.question: ＿＿によると、{今日|きょう}は{午後|ごご}から{雨|あめ}らしい。
quiz_more.en: According to the forecast, it'll rain from the afternoon.
quiz_more.explain: によると cites an outside source. For your own view, say 私は〜と思う, never 私によると.

kanji.where: The green sign with a running man above the classroom door: the door you ran to.
kanji.breakdown: {非常口|ひじょうぐち}: 非 not + 常 usual → {非常|ひじょう} 'emergency', + 口 mouth, opening → 'the emergency opening'.
kanji.related: {非常ベル|ひじょうベル} = fire alarm bell; {出口|でぐち} = exit.

tip.title: Don't run, duck
tip.body: Every phone in the room plays the same chime a few seconds before strong shaking: the {緊急地震速報|きんきゅうじしんそくほう} (earthquake early warning). The Japanese rule is the opposite of instinct: don't run outside, get under a table and hold on. The free 'Safety tips' app from Japan's tourism agency gives these alerts in English.

challenge.prompt: {健太|けんた} on LINE: 「{明日|あした}、{白馬|はくば}{行こう|いこう}かな{思てん|おもてん}ねんけど、{天気|てんき}どうなん？」 You saw a forecast of {大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}. Tell him what it says and give him advice.
challenge.hint: 〜によると…らしい · 〜ないほうがいい
challenge.model_answer: {天気予報|てんきよほう|weather forecast|3}によると、{明日|あした}は{大雪|おおゆき|heavy snow|3}らしいよ。{車|くるま}で{行かない|いかない}ほうがいいと{思う|おもう}。
challenge.explanation: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると names your source, and らしい marks it as something you heard, not your own claim. 〜ないほうがいいと{思|おも}う gives advice gently. Plain form and よ suit a friend on LINE.

vocab.note: {地|じ} ground + {震|しん} quake. {地震|じしん}だ！ is what everyone shouts.
{逃|に}げなきゃ = {逃|に}げなければ: I have to get away!
Secondary school pupils. University students are {学生|がくせい}.
Opens a confession or surprise: {実|じつ}は… = to tell the truth…
{避難|ひなん} evacuation + {訓練|くんれん} training. Every Japanese school does them.
{揺|ゆ}れてる！ = it's shaking! Also trains and hearts: {心|こころ}が{揺|ゆ}れる.
{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて！ = calm down! Also: a cosy place is {落|お}ち{着|つ}く.
{非常用|ひじょうよう} = for emergencies, {非常口|ひじょうぐち} = emergency exit.
{停|てい} stop + {電|でん} electricity. Common after snowstorms in the mountains.

kanji_study.parts: 雨 rain on top + 辰 (an old sign tied to thunder) → thunder in a storm that makes the ground shake: quake.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 振 (wave, shake by hand): 振 has 扌 hand on the left, 震 has 雨 rain on top.

kanji_study.parts: Originally a picture of a bent, woven basket → bend. A melody bends up and down, so it also means a tune.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 典 (rule, ceremony): 典 has two legs (八) at the bottom, 曲 doesn't.

extras.title: Earthquake words
extras.intro: What you'll hear on TV and the town loudspeakers after a quake.

items.note: Japan's 0–7 shaking scale. 3 rattles the dishes; 5 and up is serious.

items.jp: {余震|よしん|aftershock|3}に{注意|ちゅうい}してください
items.note: Heard after every bigger quake, for days.

items.jp: この{地震|じしん|earthquake|4}による{津波|つなみ|tsunami|3}の{心配|しんぱい}はありません
items.en: There is no tsunami risk from this earthquake
items.note: The sentence everyone waits for on the news.
Usually a school gym or community hall. Check yours on the town map.

extras.title: Three ways to give advice
extras.title_jp: アドバイスの{言い方|いいかた}

items.jp: {外|そと}に{出ない|でない}ほうがいいよ。
items.note: 〜ほうがいい: clear advice. Can sound strong to a superior.

items.jp: {水|みず}を{買って|かって}おくといいよ。
items.en: It's good to buy some water.
items.note: 〜といい: a friendly tip, 'it helps if…'.

items.jp: {先生|せんせい}に{聞いて|きいて}みたら？
items.en: Why don't you ask the teacher?
items.note: 〜たら？: a light suggestion between friends.
